name: SysML v2 Target Notation for Turing Generator MVP
purpose: Defines the deliberately limited SysML v2 textual notation subset that Phase J of the Turing Generator MVP is allowed to serialize deterministically from one validated explicit Internal Engineering Model snapshot for later SYSIDE validation.
scope_principle: The MVP reduces scope by limiting the generated SysML v2 language subset, not by accepting invalid syntax.

target_notation_status.extension_policy: Any additional SysML v2 construct must be supported by the local SysML v2 specification/release reference, validated through a small SYSIDE syntax fixture, intentionally added to allowed_constructs, and explicitly mapped by the Generation Profile before production generation may use it.

allowed_constructs.name: Package
usage_rules: Use packages for top-level and nested model organization.
Use clear package names that reflect the model area.
Avoid deeply nested package structures in MVP output unless required.

allowed_constructs.name: Documentation block
allowed_constructs.purpose: Capture human-readable rationale, traceability, assumptions and review notes.
usage_rules: Use doc blocks for rationale and traceability where formal cross-file references are intentionally avoided.
Use doc blocks to preserve source references, recipe IDs, agent personality IDs and human decision IDs.
Do not use documentation blocks as a substitute for validation.
allowed_constructs.example: doc /* This element was generated from approved model data. */

allowed_constructs.name: Part definition
usage_rules: Use part definitions for logical or physical components.
Use singular, descriptive names.
Avoid implementation-specific file or class names in logical model output.

Use part definitions for Human-reviewed standalone reusable stakeholder-role types only when Target-Model Formulation authority explicitly selects TN_003 and validated syntax-fixture evidence is bound.

supporting_reference_paths: sysml/src/training/35. Use Cases/Use Case Definition Example.sysml
syntax_evidence.authority_note: The fixture validates standalone Part Definition syntax only. Human authority is still required before any stakeholder element is materialized through TN_003.

allowed_constructs.name: Part usage
allowed_constructs.purpose: Represent one individual structural component occurrence/feature.
usage_rules: Use part usages for individual logical or physical IEM components.
Use the stable generated IME symbol as the usage identity.
Do not create a reusable Part Definition unless a separate reviewed type concept exists.

allowed_constructs.name: Action definition
allowed_constructs.purpose: Define reusable system functions or workflow capabilities.
usage_rules: Use action definitions for system-level functions.
Use verb-object names such as IngestLegacyData or GenerateSysMLv2Artifacts.
Do not model Python functions as action definitions on system level.

allowed_constructs.name: Action usage
allowed_constructs.purpose: Represent one individual system or subsystem function occurrence/feature.
usage_rules: Use action usages for individual reviewed IEM functions.
Use the stable generated IME symbol as the usage identity.
Do not create a reusable Action Definition unless a separate reviewed type concept exists.

allowed_constructs.name: Requirement definition
allowed_constructs.purpose: Define reusable requirement categories in manually curated architecture model files.
usage_rules: Use requirement definitions for requirement categories.
Use this construct primarily in architecture model files.
Generated model output may use a smaller requirement subset.

allowed_constructs.name: Requirement usage
allowed_constructs.purpose: Represent one individual reviewed requirement in generated target-model output.
usage_rules: Use Requirement Usage for individual IEM requirements.
Use the stable generated technical symbol as the textual identity.
Project requirement description through a safe documentation block.
Do not invent a subject, base Requirement Definition or constraint semantics that are absent from the reviewed IEM.

syntax_evidence.evidence_scope: The satisfaction fixture contains a simple requirement usage that was opened and visualized without observed errors.

allowed_constructs.name: Simple specialization
allowed_constructs.purpose: Define more specific element types from a base type.
usage_rules: Use only simple one-level specialization in generated MVP output.
Avoid complex inheritance hierarchies.
Use specialization only when it improves model clarity.

allowed_constructs.name: Qualified reference
usage_rules: Use qualified references when definitions are stored in a separate package.
Keep package names stable.
Validate quoted package names in the selected SysML v2 environment before relying on them for generated output.

allowed_constructs.name: Item definition
allowed_constructs.purpose: Define relevant data or artifact types exchanged in the workflow.
usage_rules: Use item definitions for important data or artifact concepts.
Use item definitions for model-level concepts, not for every physical file.
Keep item definitions stable and reviewable.

allowed_constructs.name: Use Case Definition
allowed_constructs.purpose: Represent an explicitly modeled use-case definition.
usage_rules: Use only for IEM semantics explicitly mapped to this construct by the Generation Profile.
Do not infer subject, actors, objectives or included use cases when they are not represented by supported reviewed semantics.
The J1 syntax evidence validates the construct form; production mapping remains a J2 responsibility.

syntax_evidence.source_reference_path: sysml/src/training/35. Use Cases/Use Case Definition Example.sysml

allowed_constructs.name: Dependency Relationship
allowed_constructs.purpose: Represent an explicitly mapped directed dependency between generated model elements.
usage_rules: Use only when the Generation Profile explicitly maps the exact IEM relationship semantics to dependency.
Preserve source-to-target directionality.
Do not use dependency as a fallback for unsupported relationship semantics.

allowed_constructs.name: Allocation Relationship
allowed_constructs.purpose: Represent an explicitly mapped allocation between generated model elements.
usage_rules: Use only when the Generation Profile explicitly maps the exact IEM relationship semantics to allocation.
Preserve the accepted source and target endpoints.
Do not infer allocation merely from package placement or model-area proximity.

allowed_constructs.name: Satisfy Requirement Relationship
allowed_constructs.purpose: Represent an explicitly mapped satisfaction relationship between a requirement and its satisfying element.
usage_rules: Use only when the Generation Profile explicitly maps the exact IEM relationship semantics to satisfaction.
Preserve the reviewed relationship direction and endpoints.
Do not replace unsupported refinement or traceability semantics with satisfy.

restricted_constructs.name: Advanced ports and interfaces
restricted_constructs.reason: Interface and port modeling is outside the initial MVP target notation.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Do not generate unless explicitly added to the target notation after validation.

restricted_constructs.name: Advanced item flows
restricted_constructs.reason: Formal item flow modeling is not required for the first MVP.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Represent artifact flow in doc blocks or JSON traceability records for the MVP.

restricted_constructs.name: Advanced constraint modeling
restricted_constructs.reason: Formal constraint modeling is beyond the initial MVP scope.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Use requirement or doc-based constraints in the MVP unless formal constraints are explicitly introduced later.

restricted_constructs.name: Advanced verification modeling
restricted_constructs.reason: The MVP prepares validation artifacts but does not generate a full verification model.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Store validation findings as reviewable artifacts instead.

restricted_constructs.name: Complex behavioral control flow
restricted_constructs.reason: The MVP uses textual workflow descriptions in doc blocks rather than full formal execution semantics.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Use action definitions and action usages with doc-based flow descriptions.

restricted_constructs.name: Deep cross-file formal references
restricted_constructs.reason: Cross-file references may be fragile in the MVP toolchain.
restricted_constructs.usage_rule: Prefer doc-based traceability or validated qualified references.

packages.style: PascalCase or numbered package names when mirroring architecture model structure

required_doc_content_for_generated_eleme: source or input reference where applicable
doc_block_style: Use stable IDs for findings, decisions and traceability where possible.
Avoid embedding large raw input text in doc blocks.
Store large source content in separate artifacts and reference it.

validation_policy.validation_rule: Phase J produces a validation-ready GeneratedSysMLArtifactSet. Small J1 syntax fixtures establish candidate rendering patterns, while Phase K validates each complete generated artifact set in the target environment before Phase L publication. Validation findings shall never silently rewrite generated output.

extension_policy.rule: Do not generate constructs outside the allowed target notation unless this file is intentionally updated.
extension_steps: Identify the required IEM semantic and candidate SysML v2 construct.
Check the primary SysML v2 specification/release reference.
Create the smallest useful syntax experiment.
Add the validated construct to allowed_constructs.
Add or update the explicit Generation Profile mapping.

syntax_evidence_policy.activation_rule: A construct becomes production-generation-authorized only after SYSIDE validation evidence is passed and the construct is intentionally added to allowed_constructs plus an explicit Generation Profile mapping.

generation_mapping_policy.responsibility: Maps exact IEM element and relationship semantics to constructs already allowed by this Target Notation Profile.
